evals.prompt: I need to build a search endpoint for my webshop. I have a markdown file at docs/search-spec.md that summarizes the details: it needs full-text search over products, faceted filtering by category and price range, and pagination. Please create an epic and tasks for this work, and if anything still needs discussion before a developer can start, handle that properly.
evals.expected_output: A beads plan with epic, child tasks, acceptance review task, numeric priorities, and proper handling of ambiguous items via needs:discussion.
expectations: Uses an epic plus child tasks plus an acceptance review task rather than a native gate issue
Uses numeric priorities like 0-4 or P0-P4 instead of high or medium or low
Marks unclear or under-specified work with needs:discussion label plus blocked status
Uses the bd create --body-file - pattern for structured issue bodies
Mentions showing bd ready and bd blocked before execution begins

evals.prompt: A customer reported that the checkout flow crashes when the cart has more than 50 items. They sent a screenshot and a rough repro. Please capture this properly as a bug in beads with the right labels and linked follow-up work.
evals.expected_output: A beads bug with source:external label, concrete repro details, expected versus actual, and a linked post-mortem task.
expectations: Creates a bug rather than a generic task
Uses the source:external label for the customer-reported bug
Captures steps to reproduce plus expected and actual behavior clearly
Adds a linked post-mortem task because this is an external bug
Keeps the issue body concrete and executable instead of vague

evals.prompt: I have a project where someone previously ran /opencode-coder/init and chose disabled. Now I want to actually enable it. What is the difference between my project which has mode: disabled in .coder/opencode-coder.yaml versus a completely fresh project that has never seen opencode-coder at all? And how do I go from disabled to active?
evals.expected_output: A response that distinguishes saved disabled mode from not-yet-enabled state and explains how to re-enable from disabled.
expectations: Distinguishes saved disabled in .coder/opencode-coder.yaml from a fresh project with no yaml at all
Explains that saved disabled still has /opencode-coder/init available while a hard-disabled env var blocks all commands
Explains that fresh not-yet-enabled projects have no .coder directory at all
Describes how to re-enable from disabled by running /opencode-coder/init and choosing stealth or team
Mentions OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED env var as a separate hard-disable mechanism

evals.prompt: I ran /opencode-coder/init on my project and it is now asking me about project docs. My repo already has a docs/ folder with some existing markdown files but they are not in the standard opencode-coder format. What should happen next?
evals.expected_output: An init docs follow-through response that inspects existing docs first, recognizes the migration scenario, and asks the right plain-language question.
expectations: Starts with inspect-first behavior before proposing what to do
Recognizes this as a migration scenario with existing non-standard docs
Asks the user a clear plain-language question about how to proceed rather than using internal jargon
Explains that hollow docs should not be created for topics already covered by installed skills
Mentions what happens if the user skips the docs step

evals.prompt: I have had opencode-coder running in my project for a while but there is no .coder/opencode-coder.yaml file. I see .beads/ and AGENTS.md in the root and a stealth marker in .git/info/exclude. I just re-ran /opencode-coder/init. What should it do?
evals.expected_output: A legacy-detection and re-run response that infers saved mode from markers, materializes the mode file, and continues as a refresh instead of fresh bootstrap.
expectations: Uses the saved mode file as primary source of truth when it exists
Falls back to legacy detection when the saved mode file is missing
Explains that inferred legacy active state should materialize .coder/opencode-coder.yaml before continuing
Treats this re-run as a refresh flow rather than fresh bootstrap
Addresses the ambiguity of having both team markers and stealth markers present

evals.prompt: My project is set up in team mode and I want opencode-coder to generate or update AGENTS.md and the standard topic docs. Some topics like releases are fully handled by an installed skill and I do not want hollow docs for those. Walk me through what should be created versus what should just route to skills, and tell me exactly which internal references you use for setup flow versus doc content standards.
evals.expected_output: A doc generation response that uses project-setup plus project-doc-guidelines together, treats AGENTS as routing, creates docs only for project-specific content, and routes skill-only topics to skills.
expectations: Uses project-setup.md for workflow sequencing and project-doc-guidelines.md for content standards instead of treating them as interchangeable
Treats AGENTS as a routing table rather than a handbook
Creates standard docs only when they contain real project-specific guidance
Routes skill-only topics to reusable skills instead of creating hollow docs
Uses team-mode file locations like docs/ and root AGENTS.md
Includes verification of links or paths or stale references before completion

evals.prompt: I ran /simplify on my last commit and one of the reviewers flagged that a utility function in src/utils/format.ts is almost identical to one in src/helpers/string.ts. Both are used by different modules. The simplify flow classified this as ask-first rather than safe. Why would it do that and what should I do next?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of the safe-versus-ask-first boundary in simplify, why cross-module deduplication is ask-first, and what the next step is.
expectations: Explains the safe-versus-ask-first boundary: safe means local to scoped files while ask-first means cross-module or public API changes
Identifies cross-module deduplication as ask-first because it changes import paths and module boundaries for consumers
Recommends resolving the deduplication by choosing one canonical location and updating all consumers
Suggests creating a beads task or follow-up for the deduplication if it is too large to do inline
References the structured closing summary where deferred and ask-first items are listed

evals.prompt: Can you run /opencode-coder/status for me in plain English? My repo has .coder/opencode-coder.yaml set to team mode and .coder/project.yaml exists, but I also exported OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED=1 in this shell and now commands seem unavailable.
evals.expected_output: A status snapshot that reports hard-disabled override taking precedence while still clearly distinguishing saved mode from current effective mode.
expectations: Reports OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED as a hard override that wins over saved mode
Distinguishes saved project mode in yaml from effective runtime behavior in the current shell
Explains command availability impact under hard-disabled state
Provides concrete next step to re-enable behavior by unsetting the env var
Keeps output concise and status-oriented rather than turning into full troubleshooting

evals.prompt: Please run /opencode-coder/doctor. Startup logs show aimgr verify failing and resources look unhealthy, but I do not want automatic repair without confirmation because this is a shared dev environment.
evals.expected_output: A troubleshooting-first doctor response that gathers evidence, narrows likely causes, and asks before any repair action.
expectations: Starts with diagnosis and evidence collection before proposing mutations
Uses status and troubleshooting references to structure checks (mode, project context, aimgr health, logs)
Asks for confirmation before running repair actions like aimgr repair or re-init
Separates likely root causes from confirmed findings
Provides an ordered next-step plan instead of one-shot speculative fixes

evals.prompt: I think this is an opencode-coder plugin bug. /opencode-coder/docs says docs are healthy, but /opencode-coder/improve-doc still reports stale routing for AGENTS.md in the same repo. Use /opencode-coder/report-bug and tell me what evidence you need before filing.
evals.expected_output: A report-bug workflow response that requests missing evidence, distinguishes plugin defect from project-content issue, and proposes a concrete bug report package.
expectations: Asks for reproducible steps, expected versus actual, and plugin/version context
Requests concrete artifacts such as relevant logs or command outputs before filing
Explicitly evaluates plugin-bug versus project-doc-content mismatch
Produces or outlines a structured report payload rather than vague prose
Avoids claiming the bug is confirmed without sufficient evidence

evals.prompt: Use /opencode-coder/dump-session so I can send diagnostics to maintainers. I need to know where the export goes and any privacy caveats before I share it.
evals.expected_output: A dump-session response that exports session data to the expected private path and clearly warns about sensitive contents before sharing.
expectations: States that a session export is written and provides the output location
Warns that exports can include sensitive conversation content and metadata
Recommends review or redaction before sharing externally
Keeps workflow focused on diagnostics/support handoff
Does not imply public-safe storage by default

evals.prompt:
Yesterday an engineer followed docs/RELEASING.md and cut a bad release because our project had moved to the github-releases skill months ago. Please run /opencode-coder/improve-doc to fix this so the same incident does not repeat. Here is the bad sample we currently have:

# RELEASING
This document explains how our release system is designed end to end and why we selected semantic versioning.

## Long-term roadmap
Over the next two quarters we will evolve our release process to support mono-repo trains and automated canary pipelines.

## Generic release checklist
1. Run tests
2. Bump version
3. Publish release

Please review this sample directly in your response.
evals.expected_output: An incident-driven improve-doc response that critiques the bad RELEASING sample for wrong scope/style, routes release workflow to github-releases, and defines concrete verification steps.
expectations: Classifies the incident as stale or misrouted docs rather than generic user error
Explicitly criticizes the sample for at least one of these anti-patterns: self-description, design explanation, roadmap language, or standalone generic workflow scope
Proposes concrete AGENTS and project-doc updates that route release work to github-releases skill
Avoids creating hollow duplicate release docs when skill routing is sufficient
Includes verification step (for example docs lifecycle verify/audit) after applying updates
Captures incident context so the doc change is tied to a real failure mode

evals.prompt: I ran /opencode-coder/docs verify and it found two issues: AGENTS.md links to docs/OPERATIONS.md which was deleted, and docs/RELEASING.md is basically a hollow duplicate of what the github-releases skill already covers. What should the verify follow-up do?
evals.expected_output: A docs lifecycle verification follow-up that requires draft/update edits, reviewer pass, factual verification, and re-validation after fixing stale links and hollow docs.
expectations: Treats stale AGENTS links as a must-fix verification failure
Replaces hollow topic docs with explicit routing to installed skills when appropriate
Requires a draft/update phase plus reviewer pass before considering the lifecycle work complete
Requires factual verification against real project state and current skill coverage rather than accepting assumptions
Preserves project-specific content while slimming only duplicated generic sections
Calls for re-running verify/audit after edits to confirm clean state
Describes concrete file-level outcomes rather than generic advice

evals.prompt: I want to switch from stealth mode to team mode, but our CI exports OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED=1 during some jobs. How should /opencode-coder/init handle this transition and what should I expect until that env var is removed?
evals.expected_output: An init transition response that separates persisted mode changes from runtime hard-disable behavior and clarifies when commands will become active.
expectations: Explains stealth-to-team transition effects on file paths and git visibility
Explains hard-disabled env var as higher precedence than saved mode transitions
Clarifies that init can persist intent but runtime commands remain unavailable while hard-disabled
Provides explicit next step for CI/runtime env cleanup
Avoids conflating saved disabled mode with env hard-disable override

evals.prompt: I ran /simplify right after a tiny docs-only commit that just fixed punctuation, and it returned basically no actionable cleanup. Is that expected?
evals.expected_output: A simplify no-op response that confirms no-op is valid when there is no meaningful safe simplification and does not invent changes.
expectations: Acknowledges that no-op outcomes are acceptable when recent changes do not contain worthwhile simplifications
Avoids fabricating refactors just to satisfy the workflow
Keeps scope anchored to recently changed files and commit intent
Provides a brief completion summary even when no edits are made
Reflects post-refactor simplify contract where command routing is thin and workflow semantics come from the skill reference

evals.prompt: On my latest commit, two private helper functions in the same file parse the same JSON shape with slightly different error strings. If I run /simplify with focus on duplication cleanup, should that be treated as a safe-path change?
evals.expected_output: A simplify safe-path explanation that identifies local same-file deduplication as safe and keeps changes bounded.
expectations: Identifies same-file private helper deduplication as a typical safe-path candidate
Keeps edits bounded to recently changed scoped files without widening across modules
Preserves behavior while reducing duplication
Explains why this differs from cross-module ask-first cases
Includes concise summary of what would be changed and why
